21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: The hub bundles this surface when a request touches `.skilled/` system code, such as a skill, agent, command, plugin, MCP server, descriptor or config. A language or authoring signal then selects the leaf, and the first leaves loaded are the shared tier under `references/shared/`. From there the router selects among four families: language references, shared patterns, the authoring and quality checklists under `assets/checklists/`, and the verifier assets under `assets/scripts/`.
24: 
25: The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
26: what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
27: loads before an intent selects it.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. INTENT MODEL
32: 
33: - **IMPLEMENTATION** — "implement / build / create / feature / component / module / authoring" requests load the five `references/shared/` pattern and organization docs, then `assets/checklists/agent-authoring.md`, `assets/checklists/command-authoring.md`, `assets/checklists/skill-authoring.md` and `assets/checklists/mcp-server-authoring.md`.
34: - **CODE_QUALITY** — "lint / format / quality gate / naming / standards / code smell" requests load `assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md`, the three `assets/checklists/js-css-style/` parts and the per-language checklists for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, shell and the four `assets/checklists/rust-checklist/` parts.
35: - **VERIFICATION** — "verify / passing / type-check / alignment drift / completion claim" requests load `references/shared/alignment-verification-automation.md` and `assets/scripts/README.md`.
36: - **HOOKS** — "session-prime / user-prompt-submit / pre-tool-use / post-tool-use" requests load `references/shared/hooks.md` and nothing else, so hook wiring stays in one file.
37: - **CONFIG** — "jsonc / .json / .jsonc / descriptor / config schema" requests load `references/config/style-guide.md`, `references/config/quality-standards.md`, `references/config/quick-reference.md` and `assets/checklists/config-checklist.md`.
38: - **JAVASCRIPT** — "javascript / .js / commonjs / .cjs / .mjs" requests load `references/javascript/style-guide.md`, both `references/javascript/quality-standards/` parts and `references/javascript/quick-reference.md`.
39: - **TYPESCRIPT** — "typescript / .ts / .tsx" requests load the seven `references/typescript/` docs: two style-guide parts, three quality-standards parts and two quick-reference parts.
40: - **PYTHON** — "python / .py / docstring" requests load `references/python/style-guide.md`, `references/python/quality-standards.md` and `references/python/quick-reference.md`.
41: - **SHELL** — "shell script / bash / .sh" requests load the six `references/shell/` docs: two style-guide parts, two quality-standards parts and two quick-reference parts.
42: - **RUST** — "rust / .rs / cargo.toml / cargo.lock / napi-rs / napi_rs / #[napi] / wasm-bindgen / wasm_bindgen / #[wasm_bindgen] / wasi / cdylib" requests load the seventeen `references/rust/` docs: seven style-guide parts, five quality-standards parts and five quick-reference parts.

11: # opencode
12: 
13: > System-code work under `.skilled/` lands with the right language standard and authoring checklist already attached, handed to the paired workflow mode without you having to know which reference tree to open.
14: 
15: ---
16: 
17: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
18: 
19: | Aspect | What you get |
20: |---|---|
21: | **Use it for** | System-code work under `.skilled/`: skills, agents, commands, plugins, MCP servers, config and runtime wiring that must hold to the sk-code standards |
22: | **Invoke with** | No direct invocation. The sk-code hub bundles this surface beside a workflow mode when it detects a system-code surface, then slices evidence by the detected language |
23: | **Works on** | The read-only evidence tree: six language standard sets, the shared pattern tier, hook contracts, alignment verification, authoring checklists and this framework's house style |
24: | **Produces** | The language-sliced evidence a workflow mode applies, plus drift-guard verification results. The surface itself edits nothing |
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 2. OVERVIEW
29: 
30: ### Why This Skill Exists
31: 
32: A task that touches `.skilled/` system code, be it a skill, agent, command, plugin, MCP server or descriptor, needs the right language rules and the right authoring checklist, not the whole sk-code reference tree. Without this surface, a workflow mode would either hold every language standard itself or guess which trio applies. A TypeScript edit would end up pulling Python and shell guidance it never needed.
33: 
34: ### What It Does
35: 
36: This surface carries the system-code evidence for the sk-code hub: language standards for TypeScript, Python, shell, Rust, config and JavaScript, a language-agnostic shared tier for naming, organization, hooks and alignment verification, plus authoring checklists for skills, agents, commands and MCP servers. Detection tries every declared specific surface first, including any operator-private surface skill, and checks this surface last as the hub's fallback. When a specific surface also matches, this surface loads as second evidence. Within it, the hub slices to the set of languages the task actually touches. Only an interop task spanning both languages legitimately loads both. The surface is read-only and advisor-invisible. The paired workflow mode owns all edits, tests and commits.
37: 
38: ### The House Style Lives Here
39: 
40: The quality and review modes ship rules that hold in any repository. This framework's own house style is a different thing, and it sits in this surface, so another repository that uses the hub does not inherit it. That covers the file layout and size limits, the `MODULE:` header, the `ceiling:` shortcut marker, the test layout, the formatter and line-length rules, the JavaScript and CSS house checks under `assets/checklists/js-css-style/` and the documentation and typing rows of `assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md`.
41: 
42: These checks load only for a file the surface detection places in SKILLED, so a SKILLED `.js` or `.css` file keeps exactly the checks it always had. The universal checklist also carries a `## 7. RULE OVERRIDES` section with one row. It replaces the review mode's TODO rule with this surface's own format: every TODO names its owner and what is left, and carries no ticket id. The section is written in the contract the other modes read, [`rule-overrides.md`](../shared/references/universal/rule-overrides.md), so a surface or repository of your own can do the same for any rule outside the hard floor.
43: 
44: ### The Language Slice
45: 
46: | Language | What the surface can operate |
47: |---|---|
48: | **TypeScript** | `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts` and `.d.ts` style guides, quality standards, quick references and the TypeScript checklist |
49: | **Python** | `.py` style guide, quality standards, quick reference and the Python checklist |
50: | **Shell** | `.sh` and `.bash` style guides, quality standards, quick references and the shell checklist |
51: | **Rust** | `.rs` style guides, quality standards, quick references and the Rust checklist split across its topic parts |
52: | **Config** | JSON, JSONC and YAML descriptor style guide, quality standards, quick reference and the config checklist |
53: | **JavaScript** | CommonJS and ESM plugin style guide, quality standards, quick reference and the JavaScript checklist |
54: | **Shared tier** | Language-agnostic patterns, code organization, hooks and alignment verification, kept in every slice |
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 3. QUICK START
59: 
60: **Step 1: Let the hub bundle it.** There is nothing to install and no command to run. When a task touches `.skilled/` system code, the sk-code hub bundles this surface alongside the active workflow mode and slices the evidence to the languages the task touches.
61: 
62: **Step 2: Read the sliced evidence.** The workflow mode loads the standards for each detected language plus the shared tier. Confirm the slice against the resource map in `ROUTER.md` section 3 before relying on it.
63: 
64: **Step 3: Run the drift guard before any completion claim.**
65: 
66: ```bash
67: bash .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/scripts/run-all-drift-guards.sh
68: ```
69: 
70: A clean exit means all four guards pass: the alignment verifier, the stack-folder verifier, the router-sync guard and the documentation claim guard. A non-zero exit reports a drift.
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
75: 
76: ### Detection and Slicing
77: 
78: Detection is two-step. First, work under `.skilled/` makes this surface the leading one when no specific surface matched: skills, agents, commands, plugins, MCP servers, config, changelogs and runtime bridge wiring. Second, file extensions and local markers select the language. `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts` and `.d.ts` map to TypeScript. `.py` plus argparse maps to Python. `.sh` and `.bash` map to shell. `.rs` maps to Rust. JSON, JSONC and YAML with graph-metadata or spec-folder markers map to config. `.cjs`, `.mjs` and `.js` map to JavaScript. When no `.rs` file is touched, local `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` markers select Rust, with napi-rs and wasm-bindgen vocabulary as intent signals. The slice is the set of touched languages, not one per task.
79: 
80: ### The Surface Standards
81: 
82: Four non-negotiables hold across the evidence. OpenCode plugins never write to the TUI. Their output goes through system-context injection, tools, append-only log files or a DEBUG-gated stream behind an env flag. Descriptors are load-bearing, since `graph-metadata.json` and `description.json` shape discovery. Alignment drift is a verification gate, so system-code changes re-run the drift guards before any completion claim. Rust preserves the TypeScript contract. The slice stays the touched-language set.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
87: 
88: ### When To Use This Surface
89: 
90: Use this surface when a task touches `.skilled/` system code, be it a skill, agent, command, plugin, MCP server or descriptor. Use it when a workflow phase needs a language standard, a language-agnostic organization pattern, a hook contract, an alignment-verification procedure or an authoring checklist. The surface is bundled, never invoked directly and never routed as a primary. Spec-folder authoring lives in system-spec-kit, not here.
91:

93:

95: |---|---|
96: | `sk-code` | Parent hub. Bundles this surface beside a workflow mode when the surface is detected |
97: | `sk-code-review` | Receives the formal findings-first review hand-off |
98: | `sk-code-quality` | Receives the author-side quality gate hand-off |
99: | `system-spec-kit` | Owns spec-folder authoring, which this surface does not cover |
100:

104: 
105: | What you see | Why | Fix |
106: |---|---|---|
107: | The drift guard exits non-zero | A language reference or router map fell out of sync with the filesystem or the machine router | Re-run `scripts/run-all-drift-guards.sh`, fix the drifted route, then re-run until clean |
108: | The expected language slice is missing | The touched extension has no entry in the surface reference map | Confirm the extension and its local markers, then check the resource map in `ROUTER.md` section 3 |
109: 
110: ---

112: ## 7. FAQ
113: 
114: **Q: Why does this surface exist as a separate skill?**
115: 
116: A: The workflow modes stay lean by owning the edit, debug and verify workflow while this surface holds the evidence they apply. One surface gives every language standard and authoring checklist a single home, sliced on demand, so a TypeScript task never pulls Python and shell guidance it does not need.
117: 
118: **Q: Can I invoke this surface directly?**
119: 
120: A: No. The hub bundles it beside a workflow mode. It never routes as a primary. For the evidence on its own, read the resource map in `ROUTER.md` or browse `references/`.

130: | Manual playbook | `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` runs the surface scenarios behind these checks |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 9. RELATED DOCUMENTS

138: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Surface contract, reference map and standards |
139: | [`references/`](./references/) | Language standard folders and the shared pattern tier |

144: | [`references/shared/alignment-verification-automation.md`](./references/shared/alignment-verification-automation.md) | The alignment-drift verifier |

133:     - Check (4): every playbook routing scenario's `expected_resource` is emitted by the router.

138:     It also checks that every surface count matches the surface modes in `mode-registry.json`, and that every file the `ROUTER.md` load-tier prose says loads on every route is in `DEFAULT_RESOURCE`.

16: Checklist for authoring or modifying OpenCode and Claude agent mirrors with safe authority boundaries, least-authority permissions, dispatch contracts, and runtime-mirror parity.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: This checklist makes agents safe to dispatch and keeps the two live runtime mirrors aligned. It focuses on authority boundaries, runtime-specific permission frontmatter, LEAF versus orchestrator behavior, and the files that must stay in parity.
23: 
24: ### Usage
25: 
26: - Use this when authoring a new agent.
27: - Use this when modifying an existing agent's frontmatter, permissions, dispatch contract, or workflow authority.
28: - Use this when converting an informal role into a runtime-dispatchable agent.
29: - Use this when updating mirrored agent files across OpenCode and Claude.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. PRE-CHECKS
34: 
35: - [ ] Read the mirrored `code` agent examples at `.skilled/agents/code.md` and `.claude/agents/code.md`.
36: - [ ] Read `sk-doc` source rules at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-agent/references/README.md`.
37: - [ ] Read the mirror checker at `.skilled/bin/check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs`; it treats `.skilled/agents/` as canonical and `.claude/agents/` as the runtime mirror.
38: - [ ] Decide whether the agent is LEAF-only or an orchestrator before granting task/delegation authority.
39: - [ ] Confirm the dispatch contract: who may invoke the agent, what inputs it expects, and what outputs it returns.
40: - [ ] Set runtime permissions to the least authority that supports the role: OpenCode agent frontmatter uses `permission:`, while Claude mirrors use `tools:`.
41: - [ ] Do not use `allowed-tools:` in agent frontmatter; current agent frontmatter uses `permission:` in `.skilled/agents/` and `tools:` in `.claude/agents/`.
42: - [ ] Identify the repo-managed mirror set: `.skilled/agents/`, `.claude/agents/`, and `.codex/agents/`. All three are live runtime mirrors — `.codex/agents/*.toml` mirrors the `.skilled/agents/` roster one-to-one, alongside `.codex/hooks.json` and `.codex/config.toml`.
43: - [ ] When adding or renaming an agent, mirror it across all three surfaces; `.codex/agents/` uses TOML (`[agents.<name>]` in `.codex/config.toml` pointing at `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`), not the OpenCode/Claude frontmatter form.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 3. STEPS
48: 
49: 1. Define the agent name, role, authority boundary, and runtime invocation contract.
50: 2. Draft OpenCode frontmatter with `permission:` fields matching the role's least authority.
51: 3. Draft the Claude mirror frontmatter with `tools:` for the equivalent runtime capability set.
52: 4. Write the workflow as operational instructions, not a copied skill reference.
53: 5. State LEAF constraints or orchestration permissions explicitly.
54: 6. Add verification expectations and failure/escalation rules.
55: 7. Keep `.skilled/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` in sync for shared behavior; retain only intentional frontmatter/runtime wording differences.
56: 
57: ---
58:

63: - [ ] grep verification for Claude frontmatter shape: `rg -n "^(name|description|tools):" .claude/agents/code.md`.
64: - [ ] grep verification that agent frontmatter is not using the command/skill field: `rg -n "^allowed-tools:" .skilled/agents .claude/agents` should return no agent matches.
65: - [ ] Mirror parity check: run `node .skilled/bin/check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` after editing agent mirrors.
66: - [ ] Verify dispatch references in commands or orchestrators point to the new agent name.
67:

14: # Config File Quality Checklist
15: 
16: Quality validation checklist for JSON and JSONC configuration files in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Specific quality checks for configuration files (JSON, JSONC). Use alongside the [universal-checklist.md](./universal-checklist.md) for complete validation.
25: 
26: ### Usage
27: 
28: Apply these checks to JSON and JSONC changes after completing the universal checklist, then use the priority levels below to determine which findings block completion.
29: 
30: ### Priority Levels
31: 
32: | Level | Meaning | Enforcement |
33: |-------|---------|-------------|
34: | P0 | HARD BLOCKER | Must fix before commit |
35: | P1 | Required | Must fix or get explicit approval |
36: | P2 | Recommended | Can defer with justification |
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. P0 - HARD BLOCKERS
41: 
42: These items MUST be fixed before any commit.
43: 
44: ### Valid JSON Syntax
45: 
46: ```markdown
47: [ ] File is valid JSON/JSONC
48:     - All strings double-quoted
49:     - Proper bracket/brace matching
50:     - No trailing commas (JSON)
51:     - Valid value types
52: ```
53: 
54: **Validation command**:
55: ```bash
56: # Pure JSON
57: python -m json.tool config.json
58: 
59: # JSONC (strip single-line // comments AND inline // comments safely)
60: sed 's|^\s*//.*||; s|\s*//[^"]*$||' config.jsonc | python -m json.tool
61: ```
62: 
63: ### String Quoting
64: 
65: ```markdown
66: [ ] All strings use double quotes
67: ```
68: 
69: **Correct**:
70: ```jsonc
71: {
72:   "name": "value",
73:   "path": "./path/to/file"
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: **Wrong**:
78: ```jsonc
79: {
80:   'name': 'value',    // Single quotes invalid
81:   name: "value"       // Unquoted key invalid
82: }
83: ```
84: 
85: ### Bracket Matching
86: 
87: ```markdown
88: [ ] All brackets and braces properly matched
89: ```
90: 
91: **Check for**:
92: - Opening `{` has closing `}`
93: - Opening `[` has closing `]`
94: - Nested structures properly closed
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 3. P1 - REQUIRED
99: 
100: These must be addressed or receive approval to defer.
101: 
102: ### Schema Reference
103: 
104: ```markdown
105: [ ] $schema reference included (when available)
106: ```
107: 
108: **Recommended**:
109: ```jsonc
110: {
111:   "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema",
112:   // ... rest of config
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ### JSONC Section Comments
117: 
118: ```markdown
119: [ ] Major sections have comment headers (JSONC files)
120: ```
121: 
122: **Required format**:
123: ```jsonc
124: {
125:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
126:   // 1. SECTION NAME
127:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
128:   "sectionConfig": { }
129: }
130: ```
131: 
132: ### WHY Comment Policy (JSONC)
133: 
134: ```markdown
135: [ ] Purposeful WHY comments only (max 3 comments per 10 LOC)
136:     - Comments explain WHY, not WHAT
137:     - Narrative comments are not used
138: ```
139: 
140: ### camelCase Keys
141: 
142: ```markdown
143: [ ] All property keys use camelCase
144: ```
145: 
146: **Correct**:
147: ```jsonc
148: {
149:   "maxResults": 100,
150:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,
151:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true
152: }
153: ```
154: 
155: **Wrong**:
156: ```jsonc
157: {
158:   "max_results": 100,      // snake_case
159:   "MaxResults": 100,       // PascalCase
160:   "max-results": 100       // kebab-case
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: ### Inline Documentation
165: 
166: ```markdown
167: [ ] Non-obvious values have inline comments (JSONC)
168: ```
169: 
170: **Good**:
171: ```jsonc
172: {
173:   "scaleDays": 90,         // Half-life ~ 62 days with this value
174:   "rrfK": 60               // RRF constant for rank fusion
175: }
176: ```
177: 
178: ### KISS / DRY / SOLID Checks
179: 
180: ```markdown
181: [ ] KISS: section nesting remains minimal and behavior-focused
182: [ ] DRY: repeated constants appear in one canonical section
183: [ ] SOLID: SRP/OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP impacts reviewed for config consumers
184: ```
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 4. P2 - RECOMMENDED
189: 
190: These improve quality but can be deferred.
191: 
192: ### Logical Key Ordering
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: [ ] Keys ordered logically
196:     - $schema first
197:     - Related settings grouped
198:     - Common settings before advanced
199: ```
200: 
201: **Example ordering**:
202: ```jsonc
203: {
204:   "$schema": "...",
205: 
206:   // Basic settings first
207:   "enabled": true,
208:   "name": "feature",
209: 
210:   // Configuration next
211:   "settings": { },
212: 
213:   // Advanced/internal last
214:   "debug": false
215: }
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Consistent Indentation
219: 
220: ```markdown
221: [ ] 2-space indentation throughout
222: ```
223: 
224: ### Section Spacing
225: 
226: ```markdown
227: [ ] Blank lines between major sections
228: ```
229: 
230: **Example**:
231: ```jsonc
232: {
233:   // Section 1
234:   "setting1": "value",
235: 
236:   // Section 2
237:   "setting2": "value"
238: }
239: ```
240: 
241: ### Value Type Hints
242: 
243: ```markdown
244: [ ] Complex values have type hints in comments
245: ```
246: 
247: **Example**:
248: ```jsonc
249: {
250:   "port": 3000,            // number: 1-65535
251:   "logLevel": "info",      // enum: debug, info, warn, error
252:   "timeout": 30000         // number: milliseconds
253: }
254: ```

264:   "featureName": {
265:     "enabled": true,
266:     "setting1": "value",
267:     "setting2": 100
268:   }
269: }
270: ```
271: 
272: ### Tier Configuration Pattern

276:   "tiers": {
277:     "high": { "boost": 3.0, "decay": false },
278:     "medium": { "boost": 2.0, "decay": false },
279:     "low": { "boost": 1.0, "decay": true }
280:   }
281: }
282: ```
283: 
284: ### Rule Configuration Pattern
285: 
286: ```jsonc
287: {
288:   "rules": {
289:     "ruleType1": { "threshold": 0.5 },
290:     "ruleType2": { "threshold": 0.3 }
291:   },
292:   "defaultRule": "ruleType1"
293: }
294: ```
295: 
296: ---

303: ## Config Standards Surface Evidence

306: - [ ] Universal standards validated in `universal-checklist.md`
307: - [ ] Findings severity/order produced with `sk-code/sk-code-review/references/quick-reference.md`
308: - [ ] Baseline security, quality, and test checks sourced from `sk-code`'s code-review mode
309: - [ ] Surface-specific deviations documented with file:line evidence
310: ```
311: 
312: ---
313: 
314: ## 7. VALIDATION COMMANDS
315: 
316: ```bash
317: # Validate pure JSON
318: python -m json.tool config.json
319: 
320: # Validate JSON and format
321: python -m json.tool config.json > /dev/null && echo "Valid"

12: ---
13: 
14: # Config File Quality Checklist
15: 
16: Quality validation checklist for JSON and JSONC configuration files in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Specific quality checks for configuration files (JSON, JSONC). Use alongside the [universal-checklist.md](./universal-checklist.md) for complete validation.
25: 
26: ### Usage
27: 
28: Apply these checks to JSON and JSONC changes after completing the universal checklist, then use the priority levels below to determine which findings block completion.
29: 
30: ### Priority Levels
31: 
32: | Level | Meaning | Enforcement |
33: |-------|---------|-------------|
34: | P0 | HARD BLOCKER | Must fix before commit |
35: | P1 | Required | Must fix or get explicit approval |
36: | P2 | Recommended | Can defer with justification |
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. P0 - HARD BLOCKERS
41: 
42: These items MUST be fixed before any commit.
43: 
44: ### Valid JSON Syntax
45: 
46: ```markdown
47: [ ] File is valid JSON/JSONC
48:     - All strings double-quoted
49:     - Proper bracket/brace matching
50:     - No trailing commas (JSON)
51:     - Valid value types
52: ```
53: 
54: **Validation command**:
55: ```bash
56: # Pure JSON
57: python -m json.tool config.json
58: 
59: # JSONC (strip single-line // comments AND inline // comments safely)
60: sed 's|^\s*//.*||; s|\s*//[^"]*$||' config.jsonc | python -m json.tool
61: ```
62: 
63: ### String Quoting
64: 
65: ```markdown
66: [ ] All strings use double quotes
67: ```
68: 
69: **Correct**:
70: ```jsonc
71: {
72:   "name": "value",
73:   "path": "./path/to/file"
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: **Wrong**:
78: ```jsonc
79: {
80:   'name': 'value',    // Single quotes invalid
81:   name: "value"       // Unquoted key invalid
82: }
83: ```
84: 
85: ### Bracket Matching
86: 
87: ```markdown
88: [ ] All brackets and braces properly matched
89: ```
90: 
91: **Check for**:
92: - Opening `{` has closing `}`
93: - Opening `[` has closing `]`
94: - Nested structures properly closed
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 3. P1 - REQUIRED
99: 
100: These must be addressed or receive approval to defer.
101: 
102: ### Schema Reference
103: 
104: ```markdown
105: [ ] $schema reference included (when available)
106: ```
107: 
108: **Recommended**:
109: ```jsonc
110: {
111:   "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema",
112:   // ... rest of config
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ### JSONC Section Comments
117: 
118: ```markdown
119: [ ] Major sections have comment headers (JSONC files)
120: ```
121: 
122: **Required format**:
123: ```jsonc
124: {
125:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
126:   // 1. SECTION NAME
127:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
128:   "sectionConfig": { }
129: }
130: ```
131: 
132: ### WHY Comment Policy (JSONC)
133: 
134: ```markdown
135: [ ] Purposeful WHY comments only (max 3 comments per 10 LOC)
136:     - Comments explain WHY, not WHAT
137:     - Narrative comments are not used
138: ```
139: 
140: ### camelCase Keys
141: 
142: ```markdown
143: [ ] All property keys use camelCase
144: ```
145: 
146: **Correct**:
147: ```jsonc
148: {
149:   "maxResults": 100,
150:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,
151:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true
152: }
153: ```
154: 
155: **Wrong**:
156: ```jsonc
157: {
158:   "max_results": 100,      // snake_case
159:   "MaxResults": 100,       // PascalCase
160:   "max-results": 100       // kebab-case
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: ### Inline Documentation
165: 
166: ```markdown
167: [ ] Non-obvious values have inline comments (JSONC)
168: ```
169: 
170: **Good**:
171: ```jsonc
172: {
173:   "scaleDays": 90,         // Half-life ~ 62 days with this value
174:   "rrfK": 60               // RRF constant for rank fusion
175: }
176: ```
177: 
178: ### KISS / DRY / SOLID Checks
179: 
180: ```markdown
181: [ ] KISS: section nesting remains minimal and behavior-focused
182: [ ] DRY: repeated constants appear in one canonical section
183: [ ] SOLID: SRP/OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP impacts reviewed for config consumers
184: ```
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 4. P2 - RECOMMENDED
189: 
190: These improve quality but can be deferred.
191: 
192: ### Logical Key Ordering
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: [ ] Keys ordered logically
196:     - $schema first
197:     - Related settings grouped
198:     - Common settings before advanced
199: ```
200: 
201: **Example ordering**:
202: ```jsonc
203: {
204:   "$schema": "...",
205: 
206:   // Basic settings first
207:   "enabled": true,
208:   "name": "feature",
209: 
210:   // Configuration next
211:   "settings": { },
212: 
213:   // Advanced/internal last
214:   "debug": false
215: }
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Consistent Indentation
219: 
220: ```markdown
221: [ ] 2-space indentation throughout
222: ```
223: 
224: ### Section Spacing
225: 
226: ```markdown
227: [ ] Blank lines between major sections
228: ```
229: 
230: **Example**:
231: ```jsonc
232: {
233:   // Section 1
234:   "setting1": "value",
235: 
236:   // Section 2
237:   "setting2": "value"
238: }
239: ```
240: 
241: ### Value Type Hints
242: 
243: ```markdown
244: [ ] Complex values have type hints in comments
245: ```
246: 
247: **Example**:
248: ```jsonc
249: {
250:   "port": 3000,            // number: 1-65535
251:   "logLevel": "info",      // enum: debug, info, warn, error
252:   "timeout": 30000         // number: milliseconds
253: }
254: ```
255: 
256: ---
257: 
258: ## 5. VALIDATION PATTERNS
259: 
260: ### Feature Toggle Pattern
261: 
262: ```jsonc
263: {
264:   "featureName": {
265:     "enabled": true,
266:     "setting1": "value",
267:     "setting2": 100
268:   }
269: }
270: ```
271: 
272: ### Tier Configuration Pattern
273: 
274: ```jsonc
275: {
276:   "tiers": {
277:     "high": { "boost": 3.0, "decay": false },
278:     "medium": { "boost": 2.0, "decay": false },
279:     "low": { "boost": 1.0, "decay": true }
280:   }
281: }
282: ```
283: 
284: ### Rule Configuration Pattern
285: 
286: ```jsonc
287: {
288:   "rules": {
289:     "ruleType1": { "threshold": 0.5 },
290:     "ruleType2": { "threshold": 0.3 }
291:   },
292:   "defaultRule": "ruleType1"
293: }
294: ```
295: 
296: ---
297: 
298: ## 6. CHECKLIST TEMPLATE
299: 
300: For formal findings-first review output, use `sk-code`'s code-review mode as the baseline and treat this file as config surface evidence.
301: 
302: ```markdown
303: ## Config Standards Surface Evidence
304: 
305: - [ ] Config standards validated in `config-checklist.md`
306: - [ ] Universal standards validated in `universal-checklist.md`
307: - [ ] Findings severity/order produced with `sk-code/sk-code-review/references/quick-reference.md`
308: - [ ] Baseline security, quality, and test checks sourced from `sk-code`'s code-review mode
309: - [ ] Surface-specific deviations documented with file:line evidence
310: ```
311: 
312: ---
313: 
314: ## 7. VALIDATION COMMANDS
315: 
316: ```bash
317: # Validate pure JSON
318: python -m json.tool config.json
319: 
320: # Validate JSON and format
321: python -m json.tool config.json > /dev/null && echo "Valid"
322: 
323: # Check with jq (if available)
324: jq empty config.json && echo "Valid"
325: 
326: # Validate JSONC (strip single-line // and inline // comments safely)
327: sed 's|^\s*//.*||; s|\s*//[^"]*$||' config.jsonc | python -m json.tool
328: 
329: # VSCode: Open file - syntax highlighting shows errors
330: ```
331: 
332: ### Common JSON Errors
333: 
334: | Error | Cause | Fix |
335: |-------|-------|-----|
336: | "Expecting property name" | Single quotes or unquoted key | Use double quotes |
337: | "Expecting ',' delimiter" | Missing comma | Add comma after value |
338: | "Extra data" | Trailing comma | Remove trailing comma |
339: | "Expecting value" | Empty or missing value | Add proper value |
340: 
341: ---
342: 
343: ## 8. RELATED RESOURCES
344: 
345: ### Checklists
346: - [universal-checklist.md](./universal-checklist.md) - Language-agnostic checks
347: 
348: ### Style Guide
349: - [Config Style Guide](../../references/config/style-guide.md)
350: 
351: ### External Resources
352: - [JSON Specification](https://www.json.org/)
353: - [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/)

18: ## 1. OVERVIEW

20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: This checklist keeps user-invoked commands consistent with the two live command architectures: contract-renderer commands and YAML-router commands. It is for commands that dispatch agents, write spec folders, route through create/spec-kit workflows, or render deep-loop contracts.
23: 
24: ### Usage
25: 
26: - Use this when authoring a new slash command under `.skilled/commands/`.
27: - Use this when modifying command frontmatter, execution paths, or command-owned assets.
28: - Use this when adding `:auto` or `:confirm` behavior through YAML execution files.
29: - Use this when changing command availability across OpenCode and Claude runtime paths.
30: 
31: ---
32:

34: 
35: - [ ] Read a YAML-router command such as `.skilled/commands/create/skill.md` or `.skilled/commands/speckit/complete.md`.

37: - [ ] Confirm command frontmatter uses the live fields `argument-hint` and `allowed-tools` when the command needs arguments or tool permissions.

40: - [ ] For contract-renderer commands, verify the rendered contract source such as `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/compiled/deep-research.contract.markdown` and workflow assets such as `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml`.
41: - [ ] Confirm command scope, required user inputs, dispatch targets, and file-write authority.
42: - [ ] Classify the command's runtime scope, then run the mirror generator. `.claude/commands` is a real filtered tree of per-command symlinks, so OpenCode-only commands must be excluded deliberately.
43: - [ ] Do not mirror commands into `.skilled/prompts/`; that path is not present in this workspace.

54: // MODULE: [Module Name]
55: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
56: ```

59: `╔═╗` box or the two-row `COMPONENT:`/`PURPOSE:` header. Files that already carry

71: ```

74: semantics; the verifier intentionally skips `.mjs` strict-mode enforcement.
75:

77:

79: [ ] No commented-out code blocks
80: ```

87: ```

94:     - No narrative comments describing obvious mechanics
95: ```

119: ```
120:

122: ```javascript
123: module.exports = { functionName, CONSTANT };
124: module.exports = functionName;
125: ```
126:

140: ```

150: ```

165:     return result;
166: }
167: ```

174:             // Deeply nested logic
175:         }
176:     }
177: }
178: ```

196: ```

201: [ ] All functions use camelCase naming
202: ```
203:

220: [ ] Module-level constants use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
221: ```
222:

224: ```javascript

226: const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 5000;
227: const VALID_TYPES = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
228: ```
229:

231: 
232: ```markdown
233: [ ] Try/catch blocks handle errors appropriately
234: [ ] Error messages include context
235: ```
236: 
237: **Correct**:
238: ```javascript
239: try {
240:     const data = JSON.parse(content);
241: } catch (error) {
242:     console.error('[PARSER] Failed to parse JSON:', error.message);
243:     throw new Error(`Invalid JSON in ${filename}: ${error.message}`);
244: }
245: ```
246:

248: 
249: ```markdown
250: [ ] KISS: avoid unnecessary abstraction or layering
251: [ ] DRY: repeated rules/constants extracted to shared source
252: [ ] SOLID: SRP/OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP violations checked and documented
253: ```
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## 4. P2 - RECOMMENDED
258: 
259: These improve quality but can be deferred.
260:

262: 
263: ```markdown
264: [ ] Public functions have JSDoc documentation
265: ```
266: 
267: **Example**:
268: ```javascript
269: /**
270:  * Validates input data against schema.
271:  * @param {Object} data - The data to validate
272:  * @param {Object} schema - Validation schema
273:  * @returns {Object} Validation result with isValid and errors
274:  */
275: function validateInput(data, schema) { }
276: ```
277:

279: 
280: ```markdown
281: [ ] Strings use single quotes consistently
282: ```
283: 
284: **Preferred**:
285: ```javascript
286: const message = 'Hello world';
287: const config = { key: 'value' };
288: ```
289: 
290: ### Async/Await Pattern
291: 
292: ```markdown
293: [ ] Async operations use async/await (not callbacks where possible)
294: ```
295: 
296: **Preferred**:
297: ```javascript
298: async function fetchData() {
299:     const response = await fetch(url);
300:     const data = await response.json();
301:     return data;
302: }
303: ```
304: 
305: ### Destructuring
306: 
307: ```markdown
308: [ ] Object destructuring used where it improves clarity
309: ```
310: 
311: **Good**:

313: const { name, value } = config;
314: function process({ data, options = {} }) { }
315: ```

698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

22: ### Location & Naming
23:

26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91:

94: ```

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

722: ### Formatting Standards
723: 
724: **Code Blocks**:
725: - Always specify language: ` ```yaml `, ` ```markdown `, ` ```bash `

736: **Lists**:
737: - Use `-` for unordered lists

740: - Keep items parallel in structure
741: 
742: **Tables**:
743: - Include header row
744: - Align consistently (usually left-aligned)
745: - Keep rows concise (1-2 lines)
746: - Use for comparisons or reference data

748: ### Writing Style
749: 
750: **Clarity**:
751: - Write for someone unfamiliar with your skill

766: - Use consistent formatting

771:

14: # Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines
15: 
16: Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Location & Naming
21: 
22: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`
23: 
24: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension
25: 
26: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
27: |---------------|-----------------|
28: | `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
29: | `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
30: | `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
31: | `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |
32: 
33: ### When to Create Assets
34: 
35: **Create an asset file when:**
36: - Templates users apply repeatedly
37: - Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
38: - Multiple examples of same pattern exist
39: - Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
40: - Template variations for different scenarios
41: 
42: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
43: - Content <30 lines
44: - Tightly coupled to workflow logic
45: - Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
46: - Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES
51: 
52: ### Template Files
53: **Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks
54: 
55: **Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
56: - Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`
57: 
58: **Structure**:
59: - One template per section
60: - Include field descriptions
61: - Show complete examples
62: - Explain when to use each template
63: 
64: **Use cases**:
65: - Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
66: - Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
67: - Code templates (functions, classes, modules)
68: 
69: ### Reference Files
70: **Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data
71: 
72: **Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
73: - Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`
74: 
75: **Structure**:
76: - Tables or lists for quick lookup
77: - Decision matrices
78: - Classification systems
79: - Standards and conventions
80: 
81: **Use cases**:
82: - Emoji selection guides
83: - File type classifications
84: - Validation rule sets
85: - Naming conventions
86: 
87: ### Example Files
88: **Purpose**: Show working examples of skill outputs
89: 
90: **Naming**: `[topic]-examples.md`
91: - Example: `optimization-examples.md`, `skill-examples.md`
92: 
93: **Structure**:
94: - Before/after comparisons
95: - Annotated examples
96: - Multiple variations
97: - Anti-patterns to avoid
98: 
99: **Use cases**:
100: - Complete skill applications
101: - Common patterns
102: - Edge cases
103: - Quality standards
104: 
105: ### Guide Files
106: **Purpose**: Detailed how-to guides for complex processes
107: 
108: **Naming**: `[process]-guide.md`
109: - Example: `packaging-guide.md`, `distribution-guide.md`
110: 
111: **Structure**:
112: - Step-by-step instructions
113: - Troubleshooting sections
114: - Best practices
115: - Common pitfalls
116: 
117: **Use cases**:
118: - Multi-step processes
119: - Advanced techniques
120: - Workflow deep-dives
121: - Integration guides
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
126: 
127: ### Title and Intro
128: 
129: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
130: 
131: ```markdown
132: ---
133: title: [Title]
134: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
135: trigger_phrases:
136:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
137:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
138:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
139: importance_tier: normal
140: contextType: general
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: 
144: # [Title]
145: 
146: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
147: 
148: \## 1. OVERVIEW
149: 
150: ### Purpose
151: 
152: [Why this asset exists]
153: 
154: ### Usage
155: 
156: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: \## 2. [Content Section]
161: 
162: [The actual template/checklist/snippet content]
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## N. Related Resources (optional, if present must be last)
167: 
168: [Links to related files]
169: 
170: ```
171: 
172: Every asset file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content, `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, and `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
173: 
174: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and OVERVIEW section.**
175: > The intro is a hook. OVERVIEW provides the details.
176: 
177: #### GOOD Intro Structure
178: 
179: ```markdown
180: # Git Commit Templates
181: 
182: Copy the template that matches the change, fill the fields, and commit.
183: 
184: \## 1. OVERVIEW
185: 
186: ### Purpose
187: 
188: Uniform messages let a reader scan history by intent instead of by author.
189: 
190: ### Usage
191: 
192: Copy the appropriate template based on commit type...
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: \## 2. COMMIT TEMPLATES
197: ...
198: ```
199: 
200: #### BAD Intro Structure (too long, has subsections)
201: 
202: ```markdown
203: # Git Commit Templates
204: 
205: Copy-paste templates for creating well-structured commit messages.
206: 
207: ### Core Principle    ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
208: Atomic commits with clear intent = maintainable history.
209: 
210: ### When to Use       ← WRONG: This belongs in OVERVIEW section!
211: - Creating new features
212: - Fixing bugs
213: 
214: ---
215: ```
216: 
217: ### Intro vs OVERVIEW Content Placement
218: 
219: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | OVERVIEW Section       |
220: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
221: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat)    |
222: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
223: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
224: | How to copy/customize | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
225: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
226: | Any H2/H3 subsections | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES                  |
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## 4. STANDARD ASSET STRUCTURE
231: 
232: **Template**:
233: 
234: ````markdown
235: ---
236: title: Asset Title - Descriptive Subtitle
237: description: One-line description of what this asset provides
238: trigger_phrases:
239:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
240:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
241:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
242: importance_tier: normal
243: contextType: general

250: 
251: \## 1. OVERVIEW
252:

254: 
255: [Why this asset exists, what problem it solves]
256: 
257: ### Usage

259: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
260: 
261: ---

263: \## 2. SECTION NAME

265: **Key Points**:
266: - Point 1
267: - Point 2
268: - Point 3
269: 
270: **Template**:
271: ```[language]

274: ```
275: 
276: **Field Guidelines**:
277: 
278: **`field_name`**:
279: - Description of field
280: - Format requirements
281: - Example: `value-example`

301: ````

304: 
305: ## 5. LOGIC REPRESENTATION PATTERNS
306: 
307: **Purpose**: Guidelines for representing logic, workflows, and decision trees in asset files using structured formats instead of prose.
308: 
309: **Why Structured Logic?**
310: - **Clarity**: Executable-style logic is easier to understand than prose
311: - **AI-Friendly**: LLMs parse structured logic better than narrative descriptions
312: - **Maintainability**: Changes to logic are more visible in structured formats
313: - **Consistency**: Same patterns across all asset files
314: 
315: ### When to Use Each Format
316: 
317: **Use Python Pseudo-Code When:**
318: - Complex branching logic (multiple IF/ELIF/ELSE conditions)
319: - Function/method definitions with clear inputs/outputs
320: - State management or algorithmic processes
321: - Validation or transformation logic
322: - Examples: Mode detection, validation pipelines, decision functions
323: 
324: **Use YAML Structures When:**
325: - Configuration data (settings, options, parameters)
326: - Pipeline definitions (multi-step workflows with clear phases)
327: - Hierarchical workflows (nested processes)
328: - Metadata structures (categorization, tagging)
329: - Examples: Workflow definitions, configuration templates, feature matrices
330: 
331: **Use Markdown Decision Trees When:**
332: - Simple branching logic (2-5 branches)
333: - Visual flow representation (user-facing paths)
334: - Classification systems (type determination)
335: - Quick decision guides
336: - Examples: Document type selection, frontmatter requirements
337: 
338: **Keep Markdown Prose When:**
339: - Explanatory text and conceptual overviews
340: - Narrative examples with context
341: - Best practices guidance
342: - Introductions and summaries
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## 6. DECISION LOGIC EXAMPLES
347: 
348: **Purpose**: Demonstrate how to convert markdown prose into structured decision logic.
349: 
350: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Mode Detection
351: 
352: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
353: ```markdown
354: Check user input for mode indicators:
355: - If "$quick" is present, use quick mode with auto-scaling depth
356: - If "$ticket" is present, use ticket mode with depth 10
357: - Otherwise, use interactive mode with depth 10
358: ```
359: 
360: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
361: ```python
362: def detect_mode(request):
363:     """Detect execution mode from user request markers"""
364: 
365:     if '$quick' in request:
366:         mode = 'quick'
367:         depth = 'auto_scale_1_to_5'
368:     elif '$ticket' in request:
369:         mode = 'ticket'
370:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
371:     else:
372:         # DEFAULT TO INTERACTIVE
373:         mode = 'interactive'
374:         depth = 'depth_10_rounds'
375: 
376:     return mode, depth
377: ```
378: 
379: ### Markdown Decision Tree: Frontmatter Requirements
380: 
381: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
382: ```markdown
383: Different document types have different frontmatter requirements:
384: - SKILL.md files must have frontmatter with name, description, allowed-tools, and version
385: - Command files must have frontmatter with description and argument-hint
386: - Skill reference/asset files must have the 5-field block
387: - Knowledge files outside skill folders should not have frontmatter
388: - Spec files typically don't have frontmatter
389: ```
390: 
391: **After (Markdown Decision Tree)**:
392: ```
393: Document type?
394: ├─> SKILL.md             → MUST have frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, version)
395: ├─> Command              → MUST have frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
396: ├─> Skill Reference/Asset → MUST have the 5-field block (title, description,
397: │                           trigger_phrases, importance_tier, contextType)
398: ├─> Knowledge (outside skills) → MUST NOT have frontmatter (remove if present)
399: ├─> Spec                 → SHOULD NOT have frontmatter (suggest removal)
400: └─> README               → No specific requirement (usually none)
401: ```
402: 
403: ### Python Pseudo-Code: Validation Logic
404: 
405: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
406: ```markdown
407: Validate the document structure:
408: 1. Check if required sections exist
409: 2. Verify section ordering is correct
410: 3. Ensure frontmatter is valid (if present)
411: ```
412: 
413: **After (Python Pseudo-Code)**:
414: ```python
415: def validate_document(doc, doc_type):
416:     """Validate document structure and content"""
417: 
418:     errors = []
419: 
420:     # Check required sections
421:     required_sections = get_required_sections(doc_type)
422:     for section in required_sections:
423:         if section not in doc.sections:
424:             errors.append(f"Missing required section: {section}")
425: 
426:     # Verify section ordering
427:     expected_order = get_section_order(doc_type)
428:     actual_order = [s.name for s in doc.sections]
429:     if actual_order != expected_order:
430:         errors.append(f"Section order incorrect. Expected: {expected_order}")
431: 
432:     # Validate frontmatter
433:     if doc.has_frontmatter:
434:         frontmatter_errors = validate_frontmatter(doc.frontmatter, doc_type)
435:         errors.extend(frontmatter_errors)
436: 
437:     return errors
438: ```
439: 
440: ---
441: 
442: ## 7. WORKFLOW PATTERNS
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Show how to represent multi-step workflows using YAML structures.
445: 
446: ### YAML Pipeline: Document Creation Workflow
447: 
448: **Before (Markdown List)**:
449: ```markdown
450: 1. Analyze the request and determine document type
451: 2. Select appropriate template
452: 3. Populate template with content
453: 4. Validate structure and content
454: 5. Apply formatting standards
455: 6. Run quality checks
456: ```
457: 
458: **After (YAML Pipeline)**:
459: ```yaml
460: document_creation_workflow:
461:   phase_1_analysis:
462:     action: "Analyze request and determine document type"
463:     output: "Document type classification"
464:     validation: "Type must be one of: SKILL, Command, Knowledge, Spec, README"
465: 
466:   phase_2_template_selection:
467:     action: "Select appropriate template based on document type"
468:     output: "Template file path"
469:     depends_on: "phase_1_analysis"
470: 
471:   phase_3_population:
472:     action: "Populate template with user-provided content"
473:     output: "Draft document with filled sections"
474:     depends_on: "phase_2_template_selection"
475: 
476:   phase_4_validation:
477:     action: "Validate structure, frontmatter, section ordering"
478:     output: "Validation report (errors/warnings)"
479:     depends_on: "phase_3_population"
480: 
481:   phase_5_formatting:
482:     action: "Apply code standards (spacing, headers)"
483:     output: "Formatted document"
484:     depends_on: "phase_4_validation"
485: 
486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"
490: ```
491: 
492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags
493: 
494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:
495: ```markdown
496: | Feature           | Default | Description                         |
497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |

699: | Example    | `[topic]-examples.md`    | `optimization-examples.md`   |

710: **Progressive Disclosure**:
711: 1. **Introduction**: What this is, why it exists (1-2 sentences)

714: 4. **Quick Reference**: Summary at end (optional)
715: 
716: **Section Structure**:
717: - **Purpose**: Why this section exists
718: - **Guidelines**: How to use the content
719: - **Template**: Copy-paste starting point
720: - **Example**: Complete working example
721: 
722: ### Formatting Standards
723: 
724: **Code Blocks**:
725: - Always specify language: ` ```yaml `, ` ```markdown `, ` ```bash `
726: - Include comments explaining non-obvious parts
727: - Show complete, runnable examples
728: - Use placeholder values that are obviously placeholders
729: 
730: **Placeholders**:
731: - Format: `[descriptive-name]` or `your-value-here`
732: - Examples:

735:

737: - Use `-` for unordered lists
738: - Use `1.` for ordered lists
739: - Nested lists indent by 2 spaces
740: - Keep items parallel in structure
741: 
742: **Tables**:
743: - Include header row
744: - Align consistently (usually left-aligned)
745: - Keep rows concise (1-2 lines)
746: - Use for comparisons or reference data
747:

749: 
750: **Clarity**:
751: - Write for someone unfamiliar with your skill
752: - Define domain-specific terms on first use

754: - Be concise but complete

757: - Every template should have a complete example
758: - Show real-world usage, not toy examples
759: - Include common variations
760: - Annotate non-obvious parts
